title: Representing inputs as vectors
goals: Encode a record using a fixed feature order and units
Distinguish a vector dimension from the number of examples
Detect missing values and target leakage before computation
vocabulary: An ordered list of numerical components
One value at a specified position in a vector
The number of components in a vector
The recorded feature order, units and validity rules

worked_example.title: Read the same record through three stages

blocks.title: An input vector keeps an agreed order
blocks.caption: Read each row left to right, then assemble the final ordered pair. The schema explains the numbers; the vector alone does not.

blocks.label: Parcel E has width 20 mm and height 70 mm. Encode it and explain why [7, 2] is not the same input under this schema.

guided_practice.title: Convert before encoding
guided_practice.prompt: A new record has width 60 mm and height 10 mm. Give its vector in the agreed cm schema, and name one error in [60, 10].
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: The vector is [6, 1]. [60, 10] uses mm numbers where cm numbers are expected, scaling both measurements tenfold.

independent_case.title: Apply a new schema independently
independent_case.task: A new toy battery task uses [temperature in degrees C, voltage in V, age in days]. Record K has voltage 5, age 12, temperature 18. Record L has temperature 20, voltage 4, age 0. Encode both; state the vector dimension and table shape. Age zero is valid. The future failure label is also supplied in the data file: should it be appended?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: K [18, 5, 12], L [20, 4, 0]. Dimension 3, table 2 rows by 3 columns. Age zero is a valid known value. Exclude the future failure target from inputs; it is not available at prediction time.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: A and B use the same numbers but assign them to different features. Read each position by name.
Rows count examples; components count features of one example.
Whether zero is valid depends on the field. Missing means unknown, and is not interchangeable with a measured zero.

blocks.text: Read fields by name, convert to the declared units, validate, and only then write the vector. Parcel D has width 50 mm and height 30 mm. Because 10 mm equals 1 cm, its encoded vector is [5, 3]. Writing [50, 30] would preserve the numbers while changing the physical meaning by a factor of ten.

blocks.title: Optional Python check

blocks.text: This short function assumes each supplied value is a number in mm or None for missing. It is a classroom example, not a complete input validator. Trace the conversion before running it. The function represents data; it does not fit a model or predict a class.
